confirmed_errors.correct:
The travel document for a mainland Chinese resident visiting Hong Kong SAR for tourism is NOT the ordinary PRC passport. It is the 往来港澳通行证 — "Exit-entry Permit for Travelling to and from Hong Kong and Macao" (EEP), issued by the mainland Public Security Bureau, bearing a valid exit endorsement.

Per HK Immigration Department: "a Mainland resident who is in possession of a valid EEP bearing a valid exit endorsement may be landed in Hong Kong as a visitor, with a limit of stay in accordance with the exit endorsement."

Two tourism routes, by endorsement type:
1. Individual visit ("Geren Luyou", 个人旅游 G endorsement) — available only to residents of Guangdong Province and 38 specified cities. IMMD: they "are required to obtain an EEP and an 'endorsement for individual visit (Geren Luyou)' from the relevant Public Security Bureau Office."
2. Group tour (团队旅游 L endorsement) — for all other mainland residents: "Mainland residents who wish to come here for sightseeing may join group tours organized by designated Mainland tour companies."

The ordinary PRC passport supports only transit, not tourism: "Holders of People's Republic of China (PRC) passports who are in transit through Hong Kong to and from another country or territory may be granted a stay of seven days on each landing without the prior need to obtain an entry permit" — subject to holding valid entry facilities for the onward destination and a confirmed onward booking for the overseas journey.

(Distinguish the separate case of overseas Chinese, i.e. PRC passport holders settled outside the mainland: for sightseeing they must "apply for an entry permit for social and business visits to Hong Kong." Also not visa-free on the passport alone.)

The database route should therefore either be re-scoped to travel_document = EEP (Exit-Entry Permit for Travelling to and from Hong Kong and Macao) with the appropriate exit endorsement, or, if kept as an ordinary-PRC-passport route, restricted to the 7-day transit scenario only.

Source: https://www.immd.gov.hk/eng/services/visas/overseas-chinese-entry-arrangement.html (last revised 02-06-2026)

confirmed_errors.correct: required — in-person application at a government office in the applicant's own country (not an embassy/consulate, not an accredited agency). Concretely: the applicant lodges an application in person with the exit-entry administration of the public security organ (county level or above) at their place of household registration/residence, for the Exit-Entry Permit for Travelling to and from Hong Kong and Macao (往来港澳通行证) plus a tourism endorsement — "G" individual visit (Geren Luyou), available only to residents of Guangdong Province and the 38 designated cities, or "L" group tour (Tuandui Luyou), which requires travelling with a designated travel agency's tour group. Endorsement renewals on an existing permit may additionally be made via self-service endorsement kiosks or the NIA online government service platform (this online/kiosk renewal route is per the reviewer and was not independently verified). In Ellis enum terms the value should be the domestic government-office / in-person channel, never not_required; this is consistent with the route's CONDITIONAL disposition. Separate and non-overlapping: PRC passport holders merely transiting Hong Kong to/from a third country get 7 days on landing with no prior permit, provided they hold valid onward entry facilities and a confirmed onward booking — that carve-out is transit-only and must not be applied to this tourism route.

Issued by the Viet Nam Immigration Department under the Law on Entry, Exit, Transit and Residence of Foreigners (available to passport holders not falling under Article 8, clauses 1-4); purpose of entry "Tourist"; maximum stay 90 days; single or multiple entry; fee 25 USD single / 50 USD multiple; applied for at evisa.gov.vn. Alternative channel: ordinary tourist visa issued by the Embassy of Viet Nam in the USA as a loose-leaf document (sticker or loose-leaf regular visa, applied via consular.vnembassy.us or in person; no approval letter required for tourism).
